messages.author: 77d5a3e0e6f2defe
messages.subject: CRLMM support for Affy 6.0 chips?
parts:
Hello; I'm quite new to analysis of the CNV/SNP chips and totally new
to AROMA, so I apologize if this is an obvious question, but I'm
attempting to use AROMA to step through the CRLMM genotyping vignette
on some 6.0 chips we have and am encountering the following error
after the SNPRMA normalization:

Error in list(`CrlmmModel(ces, tags = "*,oligo")` = <environment>,
`throw("Cannot fit CRLMM model: Chip type to be supported: ",
chipType)` = <environment>, :

[2011-04-22 13:12:55] Exception: Cannot fit CRLMM model: Chip type to
be supported: GenomeWideSNP_6

Are the 6.0s not supported for this in Affy? Do I need to use oligo to
do this? Is this unnecessary and all this information would come out
of a CRMA/ACNE analysis (we would like to get copy number as well for
our analysis)? I searched the group archives but most of the posts
were from 2008 regarding not supporting CRLMM and since there was a
vignette (albeit for 100k/500k) I wasn't sure if that was still the
case. Thanks...

Hollis

messages.author: 185f4d4fdb048fb8
messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] CRLMM support for Affy 6.0 chips?
parts:
On Fri, Apr 22, 2011 at 1:30 PM, HWright <wri...@ohsu.edu> wrote:
> Hello; I'm quite new to analysis of the CNV/SNP chips and totally new
> to AROMA, so I apologize if this is an obvious question, but I'm
> attempting to use AROMA to step through the CRLMM genotyping vignette
> on some 6.0 chips we have and am encountering the following error
> after the SNPRMA normalization:
>
> Error in list(`CrlmmModel(ces, tags = "*,oligo")` = <environment>,
> `throw("Cannot fit CRLMM model: Chip type to be supported: ",
> chipType)` = <environment>,  :
>
> [2011-04-22 13:12:55] Exception: Cannot fit CRLMM model: Chip type to
> be supported: GenomeWideSNP_6

Unfortunately, fitting/running CRLMM in aroma.affymetrix on
GenomeWideSNP_6 is not supported/implemented.

>
> Are the 6.0s not supported for this in Affy? Do I need to use oligo to
> do this?
Yes, you need to use the oligo package for running CRLMM on GenomeWideSNP_6.

> Is this unnecessary and all this information would come out
> of a CRMA/ACNE analysis (we would like to get copy number as well for
> our analysis)?

If you want to do copy number analysis, I recommend that you use the
CRMAv2 preprocessing method which will give you locus-by-locus
copy-number estimates, which you then can pass on to segmentation
methods such as CBS. All this can be done within the aroma framework.

If you want *genotype calls* for your GenomeWideSNP_6, you need to use
oligo or another genotyping software. Note that genotype calls per se
are not needed for doing copy-number analysis/inference.

> I searched the group archives but most of the posts
> were from 2008 regarding not supporting CRLMM and since there was a
> vignette (albeit for 100k/500k) I wasn't sure if that was still the
> case.

Yes, that is still the case.

Hope this helps

Henrik
